history.summary: Pahad Mandir is Raigarh's well-known hill temple (Surya Vihar / Collectorate Marg, Chakradhar Nagar area; geocoded at 21.88733, 83.41767), famous locally as a Hanuman (Bajrang Bali) temple that blends religious faith with a hilltop vantage point. Travel vlogs describe it as one of Raigarh's famous tourist places and note it is 'also known as Hanuman temple'. A neighbouring shrine, the Shri Sankat Mochan Mandir, is often covered together with Pahad Mandir in visitor videos; the two are adjacent but documented as distinct shrines. No founding date, builder or dynasty is documented online, so it is recorded as a modern local hill shrine. Coordinates are geocoded (not survey-verified).

name: Pahad Mandir
town_description: Raigarh is an industrial city in northern Chhattisgarh, a major coal and steel hub on the Howrah-Mumbai rail line. It is also known for its Kathak dance tradition and as a gateway to the Kelo river valley.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur (~230 km) is the nearest major airport; Bilaspur (~130 km) has limited services
travel.railway: Raigarh railway station (on the Howrah-Mumbai main line)
travel.road: Collectorate Marg, Chakradhar Nagar; well connected by city roads and NH 49

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Hanuman Jayanti draws large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; typically open from morning to evening
